I5.quote: In this paper, we have demonstrated a low temperature hydrogen (H2) sensor based on reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and tin oxide nanoflowers (SnO2 NFs) hybrid composite film.

notes: Chemiresistive H2 sensing paper on rGO and rGO-SnO2 nanoflowers (200-1000 ppm H2, RT to 60 C). Measurement section: "high purity H2 gas (99.99%) was introduced at optimized concentrations by a mass flow controller (MKS, USA) while monitoring the electrical response of the sensor by current-voltage (I-V) measurement system" (main, PDF p. 3 (journal p. 2), Section 2.4). The flow controller meters gas into the chamber; no amount taken up by the sorbent is measured. Not electrochemical (no electrolyte) and not computation-only, so the I1 failure is coded no_conditions_stated per the instruction. The paper does report N2 surface areas in the SI (Figure S2: 1.74 and 5.11 m2/g, rGO and rGO-SnO2), which are not H2 uptake values. record.json is_retracted is false; no retraction statement in the PDF; the paper is a primary research article and states no prior publication of its data.
